A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PRVQL and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material. All 12 pages of each version support comparison; the supplementary pages 11–12 are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original PRVQL results on Ego4D, including validation/test performance, ablations, speed measurements and supplementary object-scale comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains the original PRVQL benchmark results, ablations, speed measurements and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The progressive architecture, AKG/SKG knowledge generation, QFR/VFR refinement, training losses and inference procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3.1–3.5 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ego4D VQ2D with the same object-scale subsets and challenging qualitative examples. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains STARK, SiamRCNN, NFM, CocoFormer and VQLoC. The test and speed comparisons retain their comparator membership, and Table 11 still compares PRVQL with CocoFormer and VQLoC across object scales.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, four evaluation metrics, 480 × 480 inputs, 50-epoch/60K-iteration training budget, batch size 12 and experimental configurations are unchanged. The supplementary scale definitions and inference thresholds also match.

E4.justification: Tables 4–10 retain the same component, stage-count, threshold, box-count, RoIAlign-size, mixing-weight and fusion-method ablations. Object-scale analysis and qualitative/attention visualizations are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Their statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–11 and the qualitative findings match. For example, PRVQL retains validation tAP25/stAP25 of 0.35/0.27, test scores of 0.37/0.28 and speed of 30 FPS.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(15) retain the same mathematical definitions and operations. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about progressive appearance/spatial knowledge refinement, novelty for EgoVQL and state-of-the-art Ego4D performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of feature refinement and experimental trends are unchanged. Appendix C retains the small-object limitation and its explanation involving downsampled frames versus CocoFormer's higher-resolution inputs and detector.

D1.justification: Implementation information, hardware, backbone, optimizer, hyperparameters and Appendix A–B architecture/inference details match. Both versions retain the same repository address and statement that code, models and results will be released.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 38 works and retain the same related-work discussion and novelty positioning. Changed bibliography back-reference page numbers reflect pagination only.

P1.justification: v2 adds James Chenhao Liang and the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory affiliation, renumbering the Brookhaven affiliation. The substantive prose, terminology and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded author block accompanies text reflow. Table 5 moves from the left to the right column on page 7, and the conclusion continues onto page 9. Figure content, captions and table structures remain unchanged; supplementary pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 updates authorship information and makes limited layout changes while preserving the scientific argument, methods, results, reproducibility information and appendices. These changes establish no meaningful net improvement or deterioration in the paper's overall quality.
